The Session

The Maid At The Spinning Wheel jig

There are 25 other names for this tune.

Also known as An Cailín Fionn, Cailín An Túirna, Cailleach An Túirne, Garrett Barry’s, Gearoid De Barra, The Hag At The Spinning Wheel, Kiss Me Darling, The Ladies’ Fancy, The Maid Of The Spinning Wheel, The Maid On The Spinning Wheel, Maire An Phortair, Nora Kista, Nora Likes Cake, Nora With The Purse, Nora’s Purse, Noran Kista, Noresnkeesta, Norickystie, Port An Achreidh, The Road To Lurgan, Sergeant Early’s, The Spinning Wheel, Tune The Fiddle, The Wild Irishman, Wreathe The Bowl.

The Road To Lurgan

Essentially a 2-part version of “The Maid At The Spinning Wheel” (or the Maid At The Spinning Wheel is a 3- or 4-part version of this tune … take your pick). One of the few tunes named after the town in whose hinterland I grew up.

A true story … I was playing this one night and somebody asked me the name. “The Road To Lurgan” I answered. A sour face … “Jayz. I’d sooner hear the road *out of* thon kip!”

↳ Posted by Aidan Crossey on September 1st, 2004.

Jerry O’Sullivan plays the fourth part as follows:

Jerry O`Sullivan & Hag at the Spinning Wheel

Will, on what recording(s) does Jerry O`Sullivan play the Hag At The Spinning Wheel?
I would like to learn this tune but have not heard any piping versions so far.

↳ Posted by gardener2 on March 23rd, 2005.

It’s on Eileen Ivers‘ “Wild Blue” cd, 2nd track. They do Maid at the Spinning Wheel, Scatter the Mud, and Jimmy Ward’s Favorite. In the sleeve notes, Eileen says she learned “the last part--the really piping, cranny, fun part” from Jerry O’Sullivan.

I’ve heard the two of them do the same set live, and they’re both just cranking on all three reels. Good stuff.

In O’Neill

This tune appears twice in O‘Neill’s ’Music of Ireland‘ (“the 1850”), as #830 ’The Road to Lurgan‘, and again (in a different setting) as #920 ’Kiss Me Darling".

↳ Posted by rwwt on February 19th, 2015.

The Road To Lurgan, X:2

This great version appears in Breandan Breathnach, Ceol Rince na hÉireann, vol. 1, 1963, p. 3, no 1 as Cailleach an Túirne.
According to the Fiddler’s Companion and Breathnach, this tune has many other names : “Cailín an Túirna”, “Garrett Barry [’s Jig]”, “Gearoid de Barra”, “Is Maith Le Nora Ciste” (Nora Likes Cake), “Kiss Me Darling”, “The Ladies’ Fancy”, ”The Maid at/of the Spinning Wheel“, ”Maire an Phortair“, “Noran Kista”, “Nora’s Purse”, “Nora with the Purse”, ”Norickystie“, ”Port an Achreidh”, “Sergeant Early’s Jig“, “The Spinning Wheel”, ”Tune the Fiddle”, “The Wild Irishman”, ”Wreathe the Bowl”.

↳ Posted by Moxhe on November 1st, 2015.

Re: The Hag At The Spinning Wheel

This lovely tune invites you to be playful and inviting you to an abundance of variations and inventions. I would like to invite you to have a listen to Fergal Scahill’s project “a Fiddle tune a day (2017)” where he in his creative and playful way is fiddling, frolicking and rollicking around with this maid ;+).
